what: S2 at full-corpus scale: post-fix native vs Python on every eval row, plus a backend control on the rows that diverged.

corpus.note: parity_check.py is row-based and uses utterances[0]; the 847 figure elsewhere counts every phrasing across these same 314 rows

model: models/knaif-qwen3-4b-v1-q4_k_m.gguf, pinned by path on both lanes (identity verified by the harness)

native.backend: vulkan (RTX 3070 Laptop, Vulkan1 — verified, not the AMD iGPU on Vulkan0)

no_regression.claim: The 84.4% is a STRICTER BAR, not a regression.
no_regression.evidence: The pre-fix baseline (2026-08-08_prefix-baseline) reported 783/847 = 92.4% on a TOOL-SEQUENCE metric. On that same metric this run scores 93.0%. Exact plan equivalence — every arg, modulo materialized defaults — had never been measured before.
no_regression.warning: Do not compare 84.4% against 92.4% or 98.3%; they answer different questions on different populations.

default_materialization.finding: A HARNESS ARTIFACT, not a defect. concat_video declares defaults:{output: combined.mp4}. Native bakes defaults into the plan envelope; Python's infer() returns the raw model plan before apply_defaults. Both render the identical command. parity_check flags it because `output` is in _SIGNIFICANT_ARG_KEYS, which deliberately refuses to excuse output-name differences.

backend_control.design: Same binary, same utterances, only the backend changed (Vulkan vs CPU). A row whose plan moves is backend-sensitive and cannot be attributed to a port difference.
backend_control.finding: The divergence is mostly DETERMINISTIC, so it is findable. S2's 60/60 Vulkan-vs-CPU control was run on a chain-heavy subset where the model is confident — the population least likely to show this effect.

divergence_attribution.sampling_ruled_out: Native takes pure argmax over raw logits (llama.rs:335, `.max_by(|a,b| a.logit().total_cmp(&b.logit()))`). Python passes temperature=0.0, and llama-cpp-python's _init_sampler takes `elif temp == 0.0: sampler.add_greedy()`; add_penalties runs first but is neutral (repeat=1.0, freq=0.0, present=0.0). Both are greedy on unmodified logits.

leading_hypothesis.claim: The remaining divergence is in the CHAT TEMPLATE / TOKENIZATION layer, not the planner.
leading_hypothesis.why: Prompt parity proves the (system, user) STRINGS are byte-identical for all 847 utterances. It does not prove the templated, tokenized sequence is. Python calls create_chat_completion(messages=[system, user]), so llama-cpp-python applies the GGUF's chat template itself; native applies its own. The plan already lists this as pinned only at the prompt-string level — this run is the first evidence that it matters.
leading_hypothesis.next_test: Dump the post-template token IDs from both runtimes for the same utterance and diff them. Cheap and decisive; no scoring involved.

mismatch_rate_by_tag.concat_video: 7/12 = 58% — 4 of the 7 are the default-materialization artifact above
mismatch_rate_by_tag.clarify: 14/74 = 19% — underspecified rows, where the top-2 logits sit closest
mismatch_rate_by_tag.strip_audio / rotate_video / bg / zh: 0% — a port defect would cluster; this does not
